tests.testName: a named lock is machine-wide: checkouts of two different repos wait on the same named lock
one process holds a named lock and the unnamed stack lock side by side
a runner started by a named-lock holder does not wait on that named lock
the unnamed stack lock keeps its lock file path, so an older copy and this one exclude each other
run --lock holds the named lock for the command and passes its exit status on
run exits 75 when the wait gives up, distinct from the command's own failure
run exits 73 naming the path when the lock dir cannot be written
run exits 73 naming /usr/bin/perl when perl is missing
a runner started by a tests-lock holder still waits on a held unnamed stack lock, under this script and under an older copy
run with no who names the run from LOCAL_STACK_LOCK_WHO, else the package.json script name
a named lock is machine-wide: checkouts of two different repos wait on the same named lock
copied-repository lock helpers execute in the requested caller checkout
with N slots, N runs hold a named lock at once and run N+1 waits naming every holder
a slots value that is not a whole number >= 1 falls back to 1 and says so
the tests lock exports BKIT_TEST_WORKERS as cores divided by slots, minus one, never below one
a killed tests-lock holder frees its slot within a second and the waiter starts
tests.reason: the existing Perl holder detects its dead parent and releases flock; the waiter polls each second (.bkit/templates/scripts/ci/bkit-machine-lock.sh:129,155).

tests.testName: taking the tests lock while holding the stack lock is refused, naming the lock order
taking the tests lock while holding another named lock is refused, naming the lock order
taking a named lock while holding the stack lock is refused, naming the lock order
a child of a stack-lock holder asking for the tests lock is refused, naming the lock order
a run with no TTY caps the lock wait at 60 s unless LOCAL_STACK_LOCK_WAIT_S is set

a 75 exit is a lock wait only when the log's give-up line names the tests lock and this run

a 73 exit with a machine-lock refusal line (lock dir or perl) is could-not-run, exit 4
tests run with a --lock-wait-s that is not a whole number exits 2 and runs no gate
tests run defaults --lock-wait-s from BKIT_LOCK_WAIT_S and rejects a bad value with exit 2
a 73 exit with a refusal line for another lock is the gate's own FAIL, never exit 4
tests run waits for a held tests lock and runs the gate once the holder finishes
tests run exits 81 naming the holder when the lock stays held past --lock-wait-s
tests run holds the tests lock for the whole gate, so a second tests run waits
tests red runs its test file without waiting for a held tests lock
tests run under CI=true never waits on a held tests lock
tests run under CI=1 never waits on a held tests lock
tests.reason: the copied template already bypasses locking under CI=1 and the current CLI runs the gate successfully.
